devices.current_help: To end this browser's session, sign out.
devices.error.bad_request: That device cannot be revoked from here. To end this browser's session, sign out.
devices.error.busy: The server is busy. Try again in a moment.
devices.error.forbidden: This session cannot manage devices. Sign in to the vault with your master password.
devices.error.network: The server could not be reached. Nothing was changed.
devices.error.not_found: That device is no longer signed in.
devices.error.reauth_required: Your master password is needed again first. Try once more.
devices.error.second_factor_required: This account has a second factor turned on, and the server cannot ask for it yet, so the devices cannot all be revoked at once here. Revoke them one by one.
devices.error.throttled: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
devices.error.unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
devices.error.unknown: Something went wrong. Nothing more was changed.
devices.forget_old.body: Revokes the apps and extensions that have not been seen for 7 days. An account can have 20 of them at once, so this makes room. Browsers are not touched: their sessions end by themselves.
devices.forget_old.heading: Forget old devices
devices.heading: Devices
devices.intro: These are the browsers where you are signed in to the web vault, one row per browser, and the devices that signed in on their own, such as the browser extension.
devices.more: {count} more were left out of this list. “Revoke all” reaches them too.
devices.revoke.body: “{name}” loses its access to the server at once and has to sign in again with your master password. What it has already stored stays on it.
devices.revoke.title: Revoke “{name}”?
devices.revoke_all.body: Signs out every other browser and revokes every app and extension. This browser stays signed in. You are asked for your master password first.
devices.revoke_all.done: Revoked: {count}. Only this browser is still signed in.
devices.revoke_all.heading: Revoke all
devices.seen_unknown: Last seen at an unknown time
devices.shares_id: This session uses the same browser id as this browser, but it is a different session. If you do not recognise it, revoke it.
devices.title: Devices
devices.what.does: Revoking takes the device's access to the server away at once: it stops syncing, its open connection closes, and it has to sign in again with your master password.
devices.what.does_not: It does not erase what the device already holds. The vault data it has stored stays on it, and so does the key that opens that data. Only a full rotation of the vault's keys, which comes in a later version, makes that copy useless.
devices.what.heading: What revoking does
devices.what.stolen: If a device was lost or stolen, revoke it here, and change the passwords it held at the services they belong to. Change your master password too if you ever typed it on that device.
